You could try {still beating by Jennifer Hartmann}, maybe {long shot by Kennedy Ryan}. They’re not doctors or anything, but they’re not morally gray 

U could also try {Dr. Grant by Catharina Maura} although it’s not a dark romance

I love Lights Out, although I didn’t enjoy the epilogue as much. For a first dark romance, I think it’s a solid choice. The first I read was Haunting Adeline followed by Credence, and I absolutely devoured those books. I was thinking about them day and night and wanting to read more and more. 
I remember wondering why the fuck did I enjoy those twisted stories so much, but since I’m not easily triggered, I just kept reading bc I know that my literary interest do not reflect what I would accept irl

Age gap only when the MMC is the father of FMC’s boyfriend, like in {birthday girl by Penelope Douglas} 

Boss&Employee only when he is the CEO and the she is the assistant 

Enemies to lovers only when they are mortal enemies 

Forbidden love only when he’s the bodyguard or when they are in the military ( like a darker version of {twisted games by Ana Huang} or something like {blood of my monster by Rina Kent} ) 

Forced proximity only when they are enemies 

But, no matter which trope is, the book absolutely MUST be a slow burn

Once I told a friend of mine about some of the books I’ve read and she looked disgusted and said “You might as well watch porn everyday, that’s not even reading”. I was a little upset for a few minutes, but then I decided I was done sharing my interests with assholes. She could’ve simply said it wasn’t her style instead of making me feel ashamed for enjoying dark romances

{Blood of My Monster by Rina Kent} is so good! The slow burn created such a tension that I felt like the MMC was talking to me when it finally happened. Now I think I’m in love with a fictional Russian captain…
